title: Terafab Update: Musk warned that the dates were highly aggressive and might not be achieved
author: Daniel Nenni
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

- First test chip: A functional SRAM chip around May–June 2027, at the Austin research fab.
- Volume production: An internal aspiration of Q3 2028 at Gibbons Creek; Musk also described Q3–Q4 2028 as possible.
- Equipment: Musk thanked ASML and other suppliers for accelerating deliveries, but did not directly confirm whether EUV machines had been ordered.
- Uncertainty: He explicitly warned that the dates were highly aggressive and might not be achieved.

Elon Musk’s Terafab project has a clearer production timetable, although major uncertainties remain. As of October 25, 2026, Musk says the Tesla and SpaceX chipmaking venture is targeting volume production in the third quarter of 2028, potentially extending into the fourth quarter. An initial functional test chip is targeted for May or June 2027 at its Austin research facility. Musk has stressed that these dates are ambitious and carry considerable uncertainty.

Terafab’s broader ambition is to combine logic chips, memory and advanced packaging within one manufacturing complex. Its official website describes an eventual output equivalent to one terawatt of computing capacity annually, supporting artificial intelligence applications on Earth and in orbit. Planned chip applications include Tesla’s autonomous driving systems, Optimus robots and space computing. These remain project objectives rather than demonstrated manufacturing capabilities.

The Texas investment provides another concrete measure of the project’s scale. In August, Governor Greg Abbott’s office announced that SpaceX would construct the main semiconductor facility in Grimes County. The first phase represents more than $16.8 billion in planned capital investment and is expected to create 3,000 jobs. Texas also extended a $30 million Texas Enterprise Fund grant, while identifying the development as eligible for its JETI incentive programme.

For observers, the distinction between announcements and operating results remains essential. The investment and employment figures describe expected development, while the official product roadmap describes intended uses. Neither establishes that Terafab can yet deliver commercial chips at its proposed scale. The next meaningful evidence will therefore be physical progress, working silicon and repeatable production. Judging the project against those milestones offers a practical way to assess Musk’s ambitious timetable without treating forecasts as completed achievements. Terafab’s significance ultimately depends on converting its substantial industrial commitments into dependable manufacturing output over the coming years.

References used for the update:

Reuters — Terafab targets 2028 for volume chip production — October 20, 2026. Production timetable, test-chip target and Musk’s caveats.
Terafab — Official website — Project ambitions, planned chip applications and manufacturing approach.
Texas Governor’s Office — SpaceX expansion in Grimes County — August 6, 2026. Planned investment, jobs and state incentives.
